item.title: Word Row: March 3
item.description: Five letters. Six chances. A whole lot of fun.

item.title: ‘Tough Times’: Honolulu Mayor Wants To Cut $50 Million For Vacant Jobs
item.description: After years of budget increases as the city emerged from the pandemic, this year the mayor proposed a lower budget than last year’s.

item.title: Let’s Fix Hawaiʻi’s Youth Sentencing Now
item.description: Second chances shouldn’t depend on luck.

item.title: Government Funds Hilo Shelter Without Safety Exits Or Fire Inspection
item.description: Hale Maluhia provides emergency shelter to vulnerable women but has never been inspected by county fire inspectors. Staff say the units are safe.

item.title: Word Search: World Capitals
item.description: Take a trip around the world with this one.

item.title: Hawaiʻi Lawmakers Should Look To New Orleans For Education Models
item.description: Rather than relying on a top-heavy state department to dictate operations, individual schools are granted full autonomy over their budgets, staffing, and curricula.

item.title: Iran War Puts Tulsi Gabbard, Regime Change Critic, In An Awkward Spot
item.description: The former Hawaiʻi congresswoman was an outspoken critic of U.S.-led regime change wars. Then she went to work for Trump.

item.title: Locals Were Crowded Out Of This Kauaʻi Beach. That May Change Soon
item.description: Years in the making, the transfer of Hā‘ena Beach Park from the county to the state is intended to alleviate longstanding parking issues and reclaim access for residents.

item.title: After A Lawsuit, USDA Agrees To Share Climate Risk Data With Farmers
item.description: Now, even if the webpages come down again, the data can remain public.

item.title: FEMA Maui Fire Aid Delayed By Top Trump Official, Senators Say
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem's policy of personally reviewing large grants held up a request to renew emergency housing aid on Maui, a new report says.
